question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**come out**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes the arrival of spring after winter.
 
• The blank needs a verb that describes buds developing into flowers.
 
• "**come out**" accurately depicts buds emerging and opening as flowers.
 
• Other options ("**take out**", "**fall over**", "**pull out**") do not fit the natural process of buds blooming.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far 1. **behind__**?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not 2. __**last **__till perpetuity. Spring 3. **__infuses __**a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds 4. __come out__ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5____ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Take out (निकालना): This implies removing something, which is not the natural development of buds into flowers.
 
• Fall over (गिर पड़ना): This means to lose balance and collapse, which is irrelevant to how flowers bloom.
 
• Pull out (बाहर निकालना): This suggests forcibly removing something, not the natural opening of a flower.
